- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >15% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward — reduce forecast lag by 1–2 days and avoid excessive dip.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 45) and sentiment is neutral/negative, model overestimates — cap forecast at 5% below recent peak.  
- When sentiment is negative and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal — adjust downward 1–2% for each negative sentiment day.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price in early part of forecast (first 5–7 days) — add 2–3% bias upward for first 5 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.7 → -0.5 → +0.7), model overfits to recent trend — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before spike.
